decision_note: Extrafloral nectary review concerns defensive plant–insect interactions outside the focal floral coordinate; no flower-mediated pollinator-antagonist trait is registered.

Focused review of angiosperm floral bracts synthesizes pollinator attraction, herbivore protection and other functions, explicitly including reinforcing and opposing agents of selection; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material.

Primary Brassica nigra study manipulates single/multiple inflorescence attackers, quantifies floral volatile responses, pollinator visitation and parasitoid attraction; retain for attack-induced floral-signal/multi-audience adjudication.

Primary Elsholtzia study measures the same volatile phenotype as attractant to effective pollinators and deterrent to herbivorous beetles/ineffective visitors; retain for multifunctional floral-scent adjudication.
Primary Phytolacca tropical-temperate comparison jointly quantifies pollination and herbivory metrics across latitudes/populations; retain for comparative multi-context adjudication.

Dissertation explicitly examines multitrophic interactions along a Brassicaceae plant-size gradient with multiple aboveground insect guilds; retain under TA uncertainty for chapter-level pollinator/herbivore and trait-axis adjudication.

Dissertation on multitrophic plant-insect interactions under belowground processes is retained conservatively for chapter-level source adjudication because the frozen query context indicates pollination/herbivory relevance not resolvable from title alone.

Primary Hawaiian lobelioid study quantifies nectarivorous bird visitation, pollen-contact vs nectar-robbing roles and plant reproductive consequences after pollinator extinction; retain for mutualism-antagonism role adjudication.

Focused book chapter on the evolutionary/ecological transition from antagonism to mutualism is retained as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material for brood-pollination and role-transition boundaries.

Primary Oenothera-Hyles study follows a pollinating herbivore across life stages, floral attraction/oviposition and plant defence, directly exposing asymmetric mutualism and herbivory costs; retain for coupled-role adjudication.
General review of natural selection in plants is too broad for the registered pollinator-antagonist floral evidence question and is not an independent focal primary study.

Focused mini-review of nectar chemistry explicitly treats attraction of pollinating mutualists and chemical protection against nectar robbers/microbial exploiters; retain as relevant multifunctional nectar synthesis.

Primary hummingbird-pollinated nectar study measures legitimate nectar removal, simulated nectar robbing and plant responses/seed set; retain and resolve report identity with SCHPRISMA-000532 at full text.
Alternate DOI/report identity for the same Biotropica hummingbird-pollinated nectar/robbing study; retain at TA stage and resolve duplicate-report status explicitly at full text.
Focused review of nectar-mediated plant-insect mutualisms covers pollination, cheating/exploitation, indirect defence and partner manipulation; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material.
Nectar-bacteria experiment measures olfactory response of an insect parasitoid; no focal pollinator response/service is measured.
Primary trainbearer study classifies hummingbird visits as robbing, theft or pollination and quantifies role frequencies; retain for consumer-role switching/boundary adjudication.
Nectar-microbe experiment measures microbial alteration of nectar chemistry and effects on pollinator consumption, but no focal plant antagonist/exploiter response is measured.
Nectar-robbing experiment uses nectar microbial community composition as the focal response; it does not evaluate a plant floral trait or plant reproductive outcome.

Primary Campsidium study relates floral morphology to nectar-robbery incidence in a hummingbird-pollinated plant and distinguishes bumblebee/bird robbers; retain for floral-trait/robbery adjudication.

Galápagos Kalanchoe study quantifies nectar robbing, floral traits and fruit set in a system where effective legitimate pollination is absent/rare; the focal study does not measure a pollinator service response.

Primary Volkameria study records legitimate butterfly/moth pollination, primary nectar-robbing bees, altered pollinator foraging and seed-set consequences; retain for pollinator-robber role adjudication.
Primary Tecoma study compares robbed/unrobbed flowers and tests effects of nectar robbery on legitimate pollinator visitation; retain for robbery-context/pollinator-response adjudication.
Primary Collaea study characterizes legitimate hummingbird pollinators and nectar robbers, robbery damage, visitation and reproductive consequences; retain for pollinator-robber/fitness adjudication.
Primary ant-plant study tests the indirect pollination cost of a defensive ant mutualism; retain for coupled mutualism-cost and pollinator-interference adjudication.
